src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2018
s: Right to Privacy is protected as an intrinsic part of Right to Life and Personal Liberty. Which of the following in the Constitution of India correctly and appropriately imply the above statement? Indian Polity: Constitutional Framework PMF IAS IP – 14
o: Article 14 and the provisions under the 42nd Amendment to the Constitution
Article 17 and the Directive Principles of State Policy in Part IV
Article 21 and freedom guaranteed in Part III
x: TH Amendment to the Constitution The Right to Privacy was recognised as a fundamental right by the 9-judge bench of the Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment K.S. Puttaswamy v. Union of India (2017). The Court held that the right to privacy is intrinsic to the right to life and personal liberty under Article 21, which is part of Part III of the Constitution of India, dealing with Fundamental Rights.

src: UPSC CSE Prelims 2021
s: 'Right to Privacy' is protected under which Article of the Constitution of India?
x: The Right to Privacy is protected under Article 21 of the Constitution of India, which guarantees the Right to Life and Personal Liberty. This was affirmed by the Supreme Court in the landmark Justice K.S. Puttaswamy (Retd.) v. Union of India judgment (2017), where a nine-judge bench unanimously held that the Right to Privacy is a fundamental right under Article 21 and is also connected with the freedoms guaranteed under other fundamental rights.

src: IAS (Pre) 2018
s: Article 21 of Indian Constitution secures
o: Right to life, personal liberty and right to privacy
x: Article 21 secures the right to life and personal liberty, and in K.S. Puttaswamy (2017) the Supreme Court held privacy to be intrinsic to them. So option 4 is correct, while options 1-3 each leave something out.

s: Which of the adopted following a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
x: The GDPR is a legal framework that establishes rules for the collection and processing of personal data of individuals within the European Union (EU). The regulation was put into effect on May 25, 2018. It requires individuals to give explicit consent before their data can be processed.

src: I.A.S. (Pre) 2019
s: Which of the following adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' in April 2016 and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018?
x: In April 2016, the European Union (EU) adopted a law on data protection and privacy for its citizens known as 'General Data Protection Regulation' (GDPR) and started implementation of it from 25th May, 2018. It replaces the EU Data Protection Directive of 1995. GDPR standardizes data protection law across all EU member countries and imposes strict new rules on controlling and processing personally identifiable informations (PIIs). This regulation also extends the protection of personal data and data protection rights by giving control back to EU residents.
